mission: Ridgeline above the new seal's hum. Torin on the edge, posture unchanged, presence diminished — warmth muted, humor gone quiet, Force-presence lighter in a way that should feel freeing and is devastating. Sera walks up and sits beside him without speaking. After a long time, his hand finds hers. Lighter grip than before. It is there.
why_now: The Sera/Torin arc has to land in an image, not a speech. The hand on a hand on a ridgeline is the final word on love without control.
conflict: There is nothing to fix. Torin is partly present and partly not. Sera does not try to fix him. The scene's argument is that presence is the thing, and presence does not require the person to be whole.
turning_point: Torin's hand finds Sera's. The grip is lighter than before. It is there.
opening_hook: Torin sits on the ridgeline with his hands resting on his knees, facing the valley where the new seal hums. His posture is the same as before. Everything else is different.
closing_hook: Sera sits beside Torin. She doesn't speak. He doesn't either. After a long time, his hand finds hers. The grip is lighter than it was. But it's there.
emotional_trajectory: Quiet grief -> the devastation of partial success -> the grace of staying

stakes.personal: Sera's arc resolved in a chosen presence
stakes.interpersonal: The Sera/Torin relationship's final note — love as presence, not as fixing
stakes.external: Torin's diminished survival as the book's living warning

setting: Veranthos — ridgeline, overlooking the valley where the new seal hums
sensory_details: Torin's diminished presence — lighter, quieter, the heavy warmth gone; Sera's face holding grief and peace without choosing between them; their hands touching in a grip lighter than before; the new seal humming in the valley below, three-part harmony audible in the Force

notes: Sera's arc resolves in chosen presence; Torin's arc resolves tragic in diminished survival. Anti-pattern: Sera and Torin do not speak in this scene; the hand is the sentence. Ben observes from a distance; interiority minimal — a single line of observation, maybe, and the rest is the wind and the ridgeline and the hum below.
